Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Trennert favors industrials, materials, hard assets and financials under a populist fiscal regime; Eisman probes inflation, valuation, private-market opacity and bank scale. Observed growth supports the directional 2026 outlook, while Fed easing had not materialized by cutoff. Their distinction between price levels and inflation rates is sound, as are conditional leverage and valuation-smoothing arguments. Claims that private credit and prediction markets are unregulated overreach. Guest forecasts and holdings remain separate from Eisman’s own views.

Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.

<a id="7SBWYjtIKTI-c020"></a>
### 020. Falling inflation does not restore affordability when the price level remains high and incomes have not caught up.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 18:20-19:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7SBWYjtIKTI&t=1100s) | Stance: endorsed | Horizon: not stated

For price P and income W, affordability depends on W/P. Positive inflation falling from 2% to 1% still increases P; absent sufficient W growth, prior purchasing-power loss is not reversed. Assumes the same relevant consumption basket.

Conditional reasoning: For price P and income W, affordability depends on W/P. Positive inflation falling from 2% to 1% still increases P; absent sufficient W growth, prior purchasing-power loss is not reversed. Assumes the same relevant consumption basket.

Assessment test: Establish whether the stated price level affordability proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.


<a id="7SBWYjtIKTI-c021"></a>
### 021. Typical workers wages remain below their 2000 purchasing-power level.

**Wrong** | Jason Trennert | explanation | supporting

[Source at 18:59-19:46](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7SBWYjtIKTI&t=1139s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Median real full-time weekly earnings were 376 in 2025 Q3 versus approximately 334-335 in 2000, and remained 370 in 2026 Q3. This standard typical-worker measure contradicts blanket stagnation below 2000; no claim that all households or housing costs improved.

Qualification: Host asks for clarification but does not explicitly endorse the long-period factual premise. Guest 2021 9% inflation dating is not separately scored as incidental.

Assessment test: Establish whether the stated real wages since 2000 proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.

- [Median usual weekly real earnings, full-time workers 16 and over](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/LES1252881600Q) (2026-10-21): Seasonally adjusted 1982-84 dollars: 2000 quarterly values 334,334,335,334; 2025 Q3 376; 2026 Q1 376 and Q3 370. Typical full-time weekly earnings exceed 2000 in purchasing power; this does not resolve every household, wage cohort or housing affordability issue.

<a id="7SBWYjtIKTI-c035"></a>
### 035. Leverage amplifies equity sensitivity to asset-value changes, so a private holding can lose value before its manager updates the mark.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 31:29-32:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7SBWYjtIKTI&t=1889s) | Stance: endorsed | Horizon: not stated

For fixed debt D and asset value A>D, equity E=A-D. A proportional asset move dA/A induces dE/E=(A/E)(dA/A), magnifying sensitivity when D>0. Rate moves alone do not fix asset value if cash flows or hedges offset them.

Conditional reasoning: For fixed debt D and asset value A>D, equity E=A-D. A proportional asset move dA/A induces dE/E=(A/E)(dA/A), magnifying sensitivity when D>0. Rate moves alone do not fix asset value if cash flows or hedges offset them.

Assessment test: Establish whether the stated private equity leverage proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.

It was regulated well before the interview.
- [Understanding prediction markets and event contracts](https://www.cftc.gov/LearnandProtect/PredictionMarkets) (2026-11-10): Regulated exchanges must maintain market-integrity and anti-abuse rules, including protections against insider trading; offshore unregistered platforms differ. These rules do not imply every informed trade is unlawful.

## Framework and tools

- Separate affordability levels from inflation rates.
- Distinguish an asset-price win from correct causal reasoning.
- Infrequent marks can conceal economic volatility without reducing it.
- Policy-regime narratives need explicit channels and counterfactual tests.
- Bank-scale arguments require integration and competition tradeoffs.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Historical valuation multiples
- Dollar index versus gold
- Price level versus wage growth
- Private-equity marks and secondary discounts
- Mortgage lock-in
- Bank deposit share and operating scale
- Prediction-market payoff comparisons

## Source cautions

Jason Trennert presents Strategas forecasts and personal holdings. Eisman questions and explicitly agrees with selected mechanisms. Backchannel agreement is not treated as adoption of every guest statistic.
- Recorded January 20, 2026, despite February 2 publication; event-relative references use recording date.
- Opening montage repeats later discussion and is not separately counted.
- Medical personal history excluded as outside investment audit.
- Host reference to Gary Marcus is not endorsement of his scaling-limit thesis.
